reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 7, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
A line of symmetry divides a shape into two ___.
samples_reviewed.correct_answer: equal halves that are mirror images

samples_reviewed.question_text: The letter 'B' has a line of symmetry. In which direction does it run?
A circle has how many lines of symmetry?
How many lines of symmetry does a square have?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency's operational method is 'identify... by drawing the line of symmetry', but all 5 samples are recall or recognition questions (counting lines on a square in seeds 42/46, naming a direction in seed 44) and none asks the pupil to place or draw a line.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Figure-type diversity is good (square at 42/46, circle at 45, the letter 'B' at 44), but the drawing-the-line sub-case the competency specifically names is never generated across any of the 5 seeds -- every item stays verbal or numeric.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Vocabulary such as 'mirror images' (seed 43) and 'horizontal (left and right)' (seed 44) is age-appropriate, and every stem is one or two short clauses well within grade 3 quarter 4 demand.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four distinct framings appear across the 5 seeds -- symmetry-line counting (42/46), fill-in-blank definition (43), letter-orientation (44), and the infinite-symmetry special case of a circle (45) -- a genuinely varied conceptual spread for one competency.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample stays specifically on line-symmetry recognition content, never drifting into the translation content of sibling node mat_g3_mg_q4_0 or the figure-completion content of mat_g3_mg_q4_2.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The discrete values shown (4 lines for a square, 'Infinite' for a circle) are the pedagogically correct counts for those shapes, not a numeric-range item requiring scale evaluation.
